AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To assess hypothesized pathways through which patient-provider communication impacts asthma medication adherence.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A national sample of 452 adults with asthma reported assessments of patient-provider communication, proximal outcomes (understanding of asthma self-management, patient-provider agreement, trust in the clinician, involvement in care, motivation), and adherence to asthma medications. Structural equation modeling was used to examine hypothesized pathways.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Significantly positive direct pathways were found between patient-provider communication and all proximal outcomes. Only positive indirect pathways, operating through trust and motivation, were found between patient-provider communication and medication adherence.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Patient-provider communication influences many desirable proximal outcomes, but only influences adherence through trust and motivation.

AbstractText.Label: PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS
AbstractText.content: To promote better adherence to asthma medication regimens and, ultimately positive asthma outcomes, healthcare providers can focus on implementing communication strategies that strengthen patients' trust and increase patient motivation to use asthma medications.
